A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pref-GUIDE study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 report original policy-training comparisons, ablations, and voting analyses using existing GUIDE human-feedback data.

after.justification: The original experiments and analyses remain, and Appendix A.1 adds trajectory-level analyses of human feedback.

M1.justification: The moving-window preference construction, no-preference threshold, Bradley–Terry objective, and population voting procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 are retained; suggested subject-specific parameters are future work, not implemented changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use Bowling, Find Treasure, and Hide and Seek 1v1 with the same 50-evaluator dataset and Top 15 subgroup. The added trajectory examples examine existing data without introducing another task, population, or test scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain GUIDE, DDPG, and DDPG Heuristic where applicable. The component-removal, binary-voting, and pooled-feedback comparisons in Figures 6–7 also retain the same membership.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces a diagnostic protocol selecting eight anchor trajectories per task and nearest t-SNE neighbors reportedly at least 100 timesteps apart. Figure 11 nevertheless includes pairs 400/380 and 150/210, making implementation of that separation unclear. Existing policy-training budgets, evaluation intervals, metrics, and evaluator groups remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3 and new Figures 10–12 extend the embedding analysis by displaying actual neighboring trajectories, timestamps, and feedback from subject 0. This tests whether nearby embeddings represent similar observations receiving different feedback. Existing policy ablations and voting analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 newly states that each experimental result was averaged over five seeds. v1 gives no seed count, so this establishes additional reporting rather than an increase in runs. No new significance tests or definitions of uncertainty bands are supplied.

E6.justification: The added trajectory analyses report new feedback examples, including Bowling feedback of 0.55 at timestep 300 versus -0.73 at timestep 411. Main performance curves, Figure 8 preference scores, and Table 1 voting percentages are retained; no same-setting performance improvement is newly reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Bradley–Terry likelihood, cross-entropy objective, window construction, and voting calculations are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding contribution summary retain the same claims about local preferences, population voting, continual learning, and superiority over GUIDE and expert-designed rewards. The additional evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly qualifies the weaker inconsistency pattern in Bowling by its shorter horizon and relatively static observations. The conclusion adds limitations concerning shared window/threshold parameters and the scaling cost of separate evaluator models, with corresponding future directions.

D1.justification: Appendices A.4–A.5 add dense-reward information concerning target visibility and distance, identify NVIDIA A100 and RTX A6000 hardware, and state that a single RTX 4070 can suffice. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish a change to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited-work membership are unchanged. Ji et al.'s multi-robot paper and CREW receive publication metadata updates, rather than becoming new references or changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering remain intact. Local changes expand Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1, replace the concluding future-work passage with limitations, add Appendices A.4–A.5, remove the acknowledgment, and add publication/review information.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains trajectory thumbnails, timestamps, feedback labels, and connecting arrows; Figures 10–12 add related appendix displays. Existing plots receive typography and spacing changes, and the algorithms reflow across pages. The main figure and table organization remains intact.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 makes the embedding-based motivation easier to inspect through actual trajectory examples and improves transparency through five-seed reporting, hardware information, and concrete limitations. These are modest gains without changed benchmark results. Their value is tempered by Figure 11's timestep pairs contradicting the stated minimum separation, which weakens the new diagnostic analysis.
